topics.title: Getting started
topics.sourceDescription: Overview of design guidance by Apple platform

topics.title: Design principles
topics.sourceDescription: Purpose, agency, responsibility, familiarity, flexibility and clarity

web.rationale: Applicable to NovaPharm corporate/Intelligence/Portal web flows: recognizable hierarchy, explicit actions, honest claims, protected user data, mistake recovery and keyboard-friendly cross-device use. This is a design review, not evidence those flows pass.

ios.rationale: Applicable to native iOS screens: preserve expected iPhone interactions, VoiceOver/touch/keyboard accessibility, clear feedback, recovery and platform-native patterns while serving pharmacy users. No physical device conformance established.

android.rationale: Applicable as shared design principles with Android-native patterns rather than copying iOS controls; preserve navigation consistency, meaningful features, recovery, privacy and accessibility. No TalkBack or signed build evidence yet.

guidelineReviewEvidence: Reviewed complete current Apple Design principles Markdown article (Purpose, Agency, Responsibility, Familiarity, Flexibility, Simplicity, Craft, Delight, Resources and 8 June 2026 change log): https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/design-principles.md.

Interpretation for NovaPharm: put product usefulness, honest medicine-data boundaries, privacy, correction/undo, understandable navigation and inclusive interaction before purely decorative Apple-like polish. Consistency must survive responsive and native platform transitions.

Review date 2026-11-19. Source-specific article review and web/iOS/Android interpretation only: no NovaPharm UI/device tests, licensed data acceptance or production release receipts were verified by this review.

topics.title: Designing for iOS
topics.sourceDescription: iPhone ergonomics, interaction and native design patterns

web.rationale: Apple's iOS-specific platform API and iPhone device-interaction prescriptions are not directly applicable to browser implementation. Shared responsive concepts are assessed under Layout, Accessibility and Design principles instead.

ios.rationale: Directly applicable: test Expo and native iOS on iPhone sizes, landscape/portrait, one-handed reach, safe areas, Dynamic Type, system appearance and iOS-only opt-in permissions. Passing source checks alone is not device release approval.

android.rationale: Apple-specific iOS widgets, shortcuts, ergonomics and API behavior are not Android platform requirements. Equivalent Android interaction guidance must come from platform-appropriate rules, though shared accessibility objectives remain relevant.

guidelineReviewEvidence: Reviewed complete Apple Designing for iOS Markdown article (device characteristics, ergonomics, inputs, multitasking, system features, best practices and related developer resources): https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-ios.md.

Interpretation: prioritize one-handed reach, primary actions, orientation adaptations, Dynamic Type, Dark Mode and explicit permission before location or biometrics. Spotlight/widgets/Shortcuts and iPhone system integrations require individual applicability tests.

Review date 2026-11-19. Source-specific article review and web/iOS/Android interpretation only: no NovaPharm UI/device tests, licensed data acceptance or production release receipts were verified by this review.

topics.title: Accessibility
topics.sourceDescription: Readable, operable experiences across different abilities

web.rationale: Applicable by translating inclusive principles into semantic HTML, keyboard-only flows, readable scaling, WCAG contrast, visible status text, alternative navigation, reduced motion and media alternatives. Native VoiceOver/Switch Control requirements need browser/accessibility-tool equivalents rather than unsupported API claims.

ios.rationale: Applicable directly to iOS/iPadOS: Dynamic Type/200% text, VoiceOver, keyboard and Switch Control, visual/nonvisual status, recommended 44pt control targets, motion preferences and on-device Assistive Access testing. None is verified merely by static Expo source tests.

android.rationale: Applicable as cross-platform accessibility intent using TalkBack, Android accessibility services, font scaling, large touch targets, alternate actions, keyboard/switch access and reduced motion. Apple-specific APIs and exact native point defaults are not transplanted to Android.

guidelineReviewEvidence: 2026-11-19 official complete Markdown article review: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility.md (Discussion, Vision, Hearing, Mobility, Speech, Cognitive, Platform considerations, resources and change log).

Source requirements recorded: larger text (aim for 200% where relevant), legible contrast in both appearances, information beyond color, VoiceOver labeling, caption/transcript alternatives, clear touch/control spacing, simpler gestures and alternatives, physical keyboard/Voice Control/Switch Control, motion reduction and Assistive Access considerations.

Platform-specific nuance: Apple's iOS 44x44 pt is a recommended default control size, not the listed minimum (28x28 pt); distinguish web CSS pixels from native points. This is an article-level review only, without device or production acceptance.

topics.title: App icons
topics.sourceDescription: Platform app icon shapes, layers and production

web.rationale: This Apple article governs system app icons, not web favicons or browser PWA icon standards. NovaPharm favicon/web manifest work needs its own web specs and logo-rights checks.

ios.rationale: Create original NovaPharm iOS app icon assets using current supported formats, variants and contrast/legibility checks; test actual SpringBoard presentation and signed app packaging before release.

android.rationale: Apple app icon layer/shape requirements are not Android adaptive/monochrome launcher-icon requirements. Produce and test Android-specific branded icons under Android guidance instead.

guidelineReviewEvidence: Official primary source inspected 2026-11-19: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/app-icons.md. Read Apple HIG App icons: recognizable product identity, layered icon variants, platform shapes, dark/tinted appearance, restrained text and current format guidance (October 2026 change log).

NovaPharm adaptation recorded distinctly for web, native iOS and Android. Not-applicable decisions exclude Apple-only APIs/resources; shared design objectives remain assessed under relevant cross-platform rules.

Evidence boundary: no corresponding website/page screenshot, assistive-technology or real-device test, asset redistribution right, signed app or protected production deployment was independently accepted in this article assessment.

topics.title: Branding
topics.sourceDescription: Express identity while preserving native familiarity

web.rationale: Applicable as adaptable brand strategy: official NovaPharm identity and restrained accent color without displacing content or hiding functional labels. Apple's App Store trademark restrictions remain distinct from web trademark law; visual acceptance still open.

ios.rationale: Applicable to native iOS: familiar system components, accessible brand accent, system legibility and original NovaPharm marks rather than replicating Apple trademarks. App Store creative rights and tested appearance remain separate requirements.

android.rationale: Applicable as cross-platform identity principle using Material/Android-native navigation rather than copying Apple widgets, with restrained red accent and accessible text; does not authorize Apple proprietary fonts or symbol redistribution.

guidelineReviewEvidence: Reviewed complete current Apple Branding Markdown article (Discussion, Best practices, Platform considerations, resources and September 9, 2026 accent-color revision): https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/branding.md.

Interpretation: maintain distinct NovaPharm tone and restrained official brand red while prioritizing useful content, system-familiar components, clear text and permitted branding rights; avoid redundant logos and brand-only launch screens.

Review date 2026-11-19. Source-specific article review and web/iOS/Android interpretation only: no NovaPharm UI/device tests, licensed data acceptance or production release receipts were verified by this review.

topics.title: Color
topics.sourceDescription: Semantic colors, contrast, brand accents and appearance

web.rationale: Applicable as design principle to public and protected web interfaces: semantic brand tokens, distinguishable interactive states, text alternatives to color and light/dark/high-contrast browser checks; Apple UIKit/SwiftUI color APIs are not web APIs. No implementation verified.

ios.rationale: Applicable as Apple-native guidance: system semantic foreground/background colors, dynamic appearance and increased-contrast support, restrained accents and actual device/lighting tests. The Expo palette source contracts alone do not verify native color behavior.

android.rationale: Applicable by adaptation of contrast, meaningful semantic color roles, distinct status signals and dark/contrast appearance, using Android conventions rather than Apple-specific UIKit/SwiftUI color APIs. No actual device conformance or release evidence.

guidelineReviewEvidence: 2026-11-19 official complete Markdown article review: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/color.md (Discussion, Best practices, Inclusive color, System colors, Liquid Glass color, Color management, Platform considerations, Specifications and change log).

Source requirements recorded: consistent semantic purpose; light, dark and increased-contrast adaptations; non-color status cues; contextual contrast for labels and maps; appropriate iOS semantic system colors; restrained tinted controls; device/lighting tests and color-profile fidelity.
Scope boundary: article text reviewed, not a certificate of NovaPharm CSS/native color conformity; physical contrast/appearance, protected sessions and deployed/signed releases remain unverified.

topics.title: Writing
topics.sourceDescription: Plain-language labels, instructions, errors and tone

web.rationale: Applicable to all public and authenticated web pages: clear and accessible field labels, concise pharmacy terminology, contextual errors, empty states and descriptive links. Individual page-copy audit is not yet accepted.

ios.rationale: Applicable to native iOS: context-specific 'tap' language, concise labels, real VoiceOver descriptions, consistent permission and medical-risk text, recovery guidance and localization. No on-device copy acceptance provided.

android.rationale: Applicable to Android-native screen copy with correct touch and system-action wording, TalkBack labels, accessible text expansion and clear error correction. No localized device-release evidence yet.

guidelineReviewEvidence: Reviewed complete Apple Writing Markdown article (voice/tone, clarity, inclusive content, labels, form hints, error recovery, device context, resources and December 16, 2025 change log): https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/writing.md.

Interpretation: maintain concise professional clinical/commercial copy with action-oriented buttons, meaningful errors beside fields, plain-language empty states, consistent task terminology and user-appropriate safety disclosures.

Review date 2026-11-19. Source-specific article review and web/iOS/Android interpretation only: no NovaPharm UI/device tests, licensed data acceptance or production release receipts were verified by this review.

ios.rationale: Applicable to native iOS research/account flows: proper keyboards, secure text entry, system autofill where allowed, validation and permission-gated data collection. No device testing or credentialed login receipt yet.

android.rationale: Applicable to Android input methods, accessible hints, early validation and Android credential safeguards. SwiftUI SecureField/TVUIKit APIs are not Android requirements.

guidelineReviewEvidence: Reviewed complete Apple Entering data Markdown article (Best practices, secure fields, required input, dynamic validation, macOS expansion tooltip, resources and change log): https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/entering-data.md.

Interpretation: minimize manual pharmacy/customer input, validate quantities and addresses early, show labels and format hints, use secure password inputs, require informed consent and never pre-fill passwords.

Review date 2026-11-19. Source-specific article review and web/iOS/Android interpretation only: no NovaPharm UI/device tests, licensed data acceptance or production release receipts were verified by this review.

topics.title: Loading
topics.sourceDescription: Communicate asynchronous loading without jarring stalls

web.rationale: Applicable to web catalogue, search, Intelligence research and protected requests: accessible loading states, cancellation/retry, async progress and preserving user actions without showing fake completion. No live latency validation yet.

ios.rationale: Applicable to iOS app candidate: system-appropriate progress, background-safe operations, responsive content placeholders and VoiceOver status announcements. BackgroundAssets details require native feasibility review.

android.rationale: Applicable to Android app candidate using Android progress patterns, accessible async feedback and nonblocking task management, not Apple's BackgroundAssets framework. Device/network recovery acceptance remains open.

guidelineReviewEvidence: Reviewed complete Apple Loading Markdown article (Best practices, Showing progress, watchOS-specific platform note, resources and 2025 change log): https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/loading.md.

Interpretation: render useful skeletons or placeholders quickly; allow non-blocking work; show determinate progress only when progress is measurable and indeterminate when it is not; never invent time-to-completion for medicine research results.

Review date 2026-11-19. Source-specific article review and web/iOS/Android interpretation only: no NovaPharm UI/device tests, licensed data acceptance or production release receipts were verified by this review.

topics.title: Managing accounts
topics.sourceDescription: Account creation, profile management and sign-in

web.rationale: Applicable to protected portal/customer access, invitation/MFA and account deletion: purpose-specific sign-in, clear recovery, data retention notices and consistent deletion experience. No authenticated tenancy or production SSO acceptance established.

ios.rationale: Applicable to iOS account UX: avoid unexpected sign-in walls, support appropriate passkey/MFA patterns, biometric labeling and in-app deletion path or direct link. Actual Cognito/Apple entitlement and signed release still require proof.

android.rationale: Applicable as account-access design intent using Android Credential Manager/biometric conventions rather than Face ID labels, plus secure MFA and deletion transparency. No Android protected-role acceptance established.

guidelineReviewEvidence: Reviewed complete Apple Managing accounts Markdown article (sign-in best practices, passkeys/2FA, biometric nomenclature, account deletion, subscription implications, tvOS/watchOS notes and developer resources): https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/managing-accounts.md.

Interpretation: justify required wholesale-only sign-in; permit public product browsing where safe; retain secure MFA; accurately describe biometric methods; provide compliant account deletion/request paths with medical-record retention caveats.

Review date 2026-11-19. Source-specific article review and web/iOS/Android interpretation only: no NovaPharm UI/device tests, licensed data acceptance or production release receipts were verified by this review.

Interpretation: foreground medicine/product search as a core action, visibly distinguish user-scoped versus global queries, offer helpful suggestions without exposing confidential recent searches, and separate iOS Spotlight from web/Android search.

android.rationale: Applicable to Android charts using TalkBack descriptions, axes, accessible underlying data tables and touch/keyboard navigation; Apple-specific Audio Graphs/Swift Charts APIs do not apply.

guidelineReviewEvidence: Reviewed Apple Charts official Markdown article (marks/axes and scale, descriptive titles, chart accessibility, keyboard navigation, color and audio graphs, platform notes and resources). Official primary URL: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/charts.md. Reviewed 2026-11-19.

Show exact values, units, time grain and source provenance; use appropriate axis scales, provide meaningful captions and accessible tabular alternatives, never convey safety conclusions solely through color.
Source article review and scoped platform assessment only; there is no independent rendered application, device, clinical data right or production release acceptance from this review.

Prefer readable labels that clearly express context/actions and semantic priority. Preserve copyability for meaningful identifiers or error messages, and use accessible secondary text rather than low-contrast decoration.
Source article review and scoped platform assessment only; there is no independent rendered application, device, clinical data right or production release acceptance from this review.

topics.title: Buttons
topics.sourceDescription: Actions with clear labels and interaction targets

web.rationale: Applicable as accessible button design: semantic button elements, keyboard and pointer operation, 44 CSS-pixel audit where agreed, visible focus/pressed/busy state and proper destructive confirmation. Native 44pt unit and SF Symbols rights do not translate into a CSS measurement standard.

ios.rationale: Direct native iOS guidance: consistent touch target size, clear label and role, iOS activity progress feedback, VoiceOver names and safe destructive action semantics; physical screen-reader and tap testing remains required.

android.rationale: Applicable as cross-platform UX goal with Android-native touch target and role conventions, pressed/loading states, TalkBack names and destructive-action clarity; UIKit/SwiftUI button APIs do not apply.

guidelineReviewEvidence: Reviewed Apple Buttons official Markdown article (control style/content/role, 44x44pt target guidance, press feedback, primary-versus-destructive roles, iOS busy button, macOS help controls, visionOS/watchOS notes, change log). Official primary URL: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/buttons.md. Reviewed 2026-11-19.

Provide recognizable action targets and visible press/busy feedback. Use prominent styling sparingly; never assign destructive action the primary role. Apple guidance quotes points for native hit regions, which is not evidence about web CSS pixel sizing.
Source article review and scoped platform assessment only; there is no independent rendered application, device, clinical data right or production release acceptance from this review.

topics.title: Search fields
topics.sourceDescription: Search input for a collection of content

web.rationale: Applicable to medicine and product catalogue search: descriptive placeholder plus accessible label, clear button, known result scope, keyboard filters, no unapproved indexed patient data and cancellable queries.

ios.rationale: Directly applicable: iOS searchable fields in top/bottom toolbars or dedicated tab, appropriate focus/keyboard behavior, scoped token filters and VoiceOver; no actual native device interaction verified.

android.rationale: Applicable as cross-platform search principle with Android SearchBar, native filters, dynamic scoped results and TalkBack; Apple SwiftUI searchable/tab positioning APIs are not Android APIs.

guidelineReviewEvidence: Reviewed current Apple Search fields official Markdown article (scope/suggestions/tokens, inline and tab search, toolbar positioning, iPad/Mac/tvOS/watchOS variants and 2026 updates). Official primary URL: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/search-fields.md. Reviewed 2026-11-19.

Expose editable, clearly scoped search fields; support dynamic relevant results, clear/Cancel affordances and accessible filter tokens, without leaking protected search histories. Pick placement by task and platform.
Source article review and scoped platform assessment only; there is no independent rendered application, device, clinical data right or production release acceptance from this review.

topics.title: Tab bars
topics.sourceDescription: Switch between top-level app destinations

web.rationale: Applicable as responsive app-navigation pattern only: semantic top-level tabs when appropriate, labels, keyboard traversal and predictable state preservation. UIKit bottom Liquid Glass tab bar is not a web requirement.

ios.rationale: Directly applicable: iPhone tab navigation, persistent top-level destinations, safe areas, labeled controls, native per-tab state and accessible overflow; actual Expo/native UIKit parity requires device proof.

android.rationale: Applicable as navigation objective with Android-native bottom navigation, navigation rail and TalkBack semantics. Do not transplant iOS SF Symbols, Liquid Glass or iPad tab-bar positioning to Android.

guidelineReviewEvidence: Reviewed current Apple Tab bars official Markdown article (top-level navigation, labels, visibility and state, no action buttons, iOS bottom tabs, iPadOS adaptable sidebar, tvOS/visionOS notes and June 2026 change log). Official primary URL: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/tab-bars.md. Reviewed 2026-11-19.

Top-level tabs are stable navigation destinations, not actions. Use concise text labels, limited primary tabs and avoid hidden/unreachable More overflow. Preserve per-tab navigation state and platform-appropriate layouts.
Source article review and scoped platform assessment only; there is no independent rendered application, device, clinical data right or production release acceptance from this review.

topics.title: Alerts
topics.sourceDescription: Communicate urgent or important information

web.rationale: Applicable to web confirmations and emergency errors: use correct dialog semantics, focus trapping/return, concise message, explicit user choice and safe cancellation. Apple native alert views are not web components.

ios.rationale: Directly applicable to native iOS alerts versus action sheets for intentional choices; verify VoiceOver announcements, destructive action cancellation, no alert storms and dismissal on actual devices.

android.rationale: Applicable through Android dialogs, snackbars and bottom-sheet conventions, not Apple's native UIAlertController; preserve minimal interruption, cancellation, TalkBack labels and critical decision clarity.

guidelineReviewEvidence: Reviewed Apple Alerts official Markdown article (nontrivial interruptive warnings, alert content/buttons, Cancel and destructive action safeguards, iOS action-sheet distinction, platform notes and change log). Official primary URL: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/alerts.md. Reviewed 2026-11-19.

Reserve interruption for necessary decision points, avoid alerting on non-actionable information or reversible routine operations, present concise situation and actionable verbs, and preserve Cancel on destructive confirmations.
Source article review and scoped platform assessment only; there is no independent rendered application, device, clinical data right or production release acceptance from this review.

topics.title: Progress indicators
topics.sourceDescription: Indicate work and loading progress

web.rationale: Applicable to long-running protected research/import and checkout operations: ARIA progress semantics, unknown-time spinner when needed, truthful completion percentages, cancellation and timeout recovery; actual browser acceptance is separate.

ios.rationale: Directly applicable: SwiftUI/UIkit-appropriate ProgressView and refresh patterns, VoiceOver status, network interruption handling and safe cancellation. No signed-device test acceptance implied.

android.rationale: Applicable using Android-native progress patterns and accessibility progress descriptions, real work metrics and cancellation. Apple's UIProgressView and UIRefreshControl are not Android components.

guidelineReviewEvidence: Reviewed Apple Progress indicators official Markdown article (determinate/indeterminate variants, accurate progress reporting, cancel/pause, iOS refresh, macOS and watchOS platform notes, resources and change log). Official primary URL: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/progress-indicators.md. Reviewed 2026-11-19.

Do not show misleading percentages for unknown-time work. Move from indeterminate to determinate only with real measured progress, show stall/retry recovery and allow safe cancellation where feasible.
Source article review and scoped platform assessment only; there is no independent rendered application, device, clinical data right or production release acceptance from this review.

topics.title: Generative AI
topics.sourceDescription: Design dynamic AI-generated experiences responsibly

web.rationale: Applicable to protected NovaPharm Intelligence research: conspicuous AI disclosure, content rights, provenance, hallucination boundaries, safe refusal/fallback and explicit consent before durable external actions. No clinical AI release proof established.

ios.rationale: Applicable to AI-powered iOS research preview: on-device versus server data clarity, user control, feedback, privacy controls and model-availability fallback. No Foundation Models entitlement/physical device validation implied.

android.rationale: Applicable as responsible cross-platform AI design intent using Android-native privacy/storage norms, no hallucinated medicine labels, explicit data rights and safe offline fallback. Apple's Foundation Models API is not an Android feature.

guidelineReviewEvidence: Reviewed complete current Apple Generative AI Markdown article (responsible/inclusive design, control, disclosure, privacy, dataset rights, input/output hallucination risks, feedback, continuous improvement and June 8, 2026 update): https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/generative-ai.md.

Interpretation: no unsupervised medical identity or treatment claims; label model-generated material and its uncertainty; preserve human decision authority, undo/refine, licensed datasets, privacy, evidence grounding and safe non-AI fallback.

Review date 2026-11-19. Source-specific article review and web/iOS/Android interpretation only: no NovaPharm UI/device tests, licensed data acceptance or production release receipts were verified by this review.

topics.title: VoiceOver
topics.sourceDescription: Support system screen-reader users

web.rationale: Applicable to Safari/macOS/iOS browser VoiceOver testing: correct semantic HTML headings, announced updates, accessible diagrams/charts and meaningful focus sequence. A source-only aria-label inventory is insufficient to verify real behavior.

ios.rationale: Directly applicable to native iOS VoiceOver: programmatically named controls, logical grouping, custom rotor navigation, predictable focus and dynamic content announcements verified on hardware.

android.rationale: Apple's VoiceOver-specific APIs and rotor are not Android OS features; Android equivalent must be independently reviewed and tested under TalkBack, accessibility services and Android UI semantics.

guidelineReviewEvidence: Reviewed Apple VoiceOver official Markdown article (meaningful element labels, image/chart descriptions, headings/navigation, grouping, change announcements, rotor, visionOS specific notes, resources and change log). Official primary URL: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/voiceover.md. Reviewed 2026-11-19.

Provide accurate role/name/state descriptions and logical headings, avoid narrating decoration, announce dynamic changes and support chart data navigation. Confirm actual screen reader interaction, not merely source attribute presence.
Source article review and scoped platform assessment only; there is no independent rendered application, device, clinical data right or production release acceptance from this review.
